caption: A geyser in a national park erupts, sending a column of boiling water and steam high into the air before it falls back.

sa.check: A geyser vent in the ground.
A column of water and steam rises from the vent.
The column reaches high into the air.
The water falls back around the vent.
Steam drifts away above the column.
The rise comes first and the fall follows.

pc.expect: The water rises from the vent, slows as it climbs and falls back down around the vent, while the steam keeps rising and drifting.
pc.fail: The water keeps climbing out of view without slowing or falling; or the fallen water travels upward from the ground; or the steam sinks and pools around the vent; or the column hangs at a fixed height without rising or falling.

pc.expect: The drops leave the vent going up and follow arcs that bend over and come down, spreading as they go.
pc.fail: The drops climb in straight lines and stop dead at the top; or the column bends sideways and stays level with nothing blowing it; or the drops return along the line they rose on and re-enter the vent; or the spray gathers into a rising ball.

pc.expect: The eruption builds and then eases, and water that has fallen back stays down.
pc.fail: Fallen water rises back into the column with no fresh eruption; or the column's height jumps up and down in steps; or the eruption stops and restarts in the same instant.

pc.expect: The water breaks into spray and drops as it rises and splashes where it lands; the steam is a soft cloud that spreads.
pc.fail: The column stays a rigid rod of water; or the spray holds a fixed shape in the air; or the steam turns into solid lumps; or the fallen water lies as a heap above the ground.

pc.expect: One vent; the water comes out of it and falls back to the ground around it.
pc.fail: Water appears in the air away from the column; or a second column rises from bare ground; or the column vanishes at a stroke while still high; or the vent moves across the ground.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The ground around the vent, its mineral crust and the background stay the same.
pc.fail: The crust changes colour; or the ground's shape changes between frames; or the hills behind change.
